title: Wash in the Jordan (2 Kings 5)
hookLine: a proud general wants a grand cure, and his servant girl's advice gets him healed

lines: A MIGHTY MAN, BUT A LEPER.
cards: In the house of a great general, a young girl waits on his wife. She's from Israel, carried off in a raid.
Her master is Naaman, captain of the army of the king of Syria, and the King James Bible sums him up in one breath: "a mighty man in valour, but he was a leper."
One day the girl says to her mistress: "Would God my lord were with the prophet that is in Samaria! for he would recover him of his leprosy." A captive, wishing her captor well.
He sets off with a letter from his king, and silver, gold and changes of clothing.

teach.b: Naaman pulls up at Elisha's door with his chariot. Elisha doesn't even come out. He sends a messenger: "Go and wash in Jordan seven times, and thy flesh shall come again to thee, and thou shalt be clean."

Naaman is furious, and the text lets us hear why: "Behold, I thought, He will surely come out to me, and stand, and call on the name of the LORD his God, and strike his hand over the place, and recover the leper."
Instead: go take a bath, in a foreign river. "Are not Abana and Pharpar, rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel?" He turns and goes away in a rage.

Then his servants come near with something wise: "My father, if the prophet had bid thee do some great thing, wouldest thou not have done it? how much rather then, when he saith to thee, Wash, and be clean?"

So Naaman goes down and dips himself in the Jordan seven times, "and his flesh came again like unto the flesh of a little child, and he was clean." Look who carries his healing to him. A captive girl.
A messenger at the door. His own servants.

teach.h: HEALED THROUGH THE ONES WITH NO RANK.
teach.b: Every step comes through someone with no rank at all. And the cure is plain water. The hard part was never the river.
It was being willing to do something that small.

how: Some Christians read Naaman's washing in the Jordan as a picture of humility and of grace that can't be earned, and some churches connect it with baptism, which in the Gospels also happens in the Jordan.

games.q: you're Naaman, a great general. you've traveled far, and the prophet won't even come to the door. he sends word: go wash in the Jordan seven times. what do you do?
o: turn away in a rage: the rivers at home are better.
wait at the door until the prophet comes out.
games.why: he goes away in a rage, until his servants reason with him: if he'd asked a great thing, you'd have done it. then he washes seven times, and is clean.

practice: Name the simple thing you've been putting off because it seems too small, or too ordinary for the size of your problem: making the doctor's appointment, saying sorry, answering the message you've left sitting, asking for help.
If part of you says, like Naaman, behold, I thought it would be something bigger, let that go by, and picture yourself doing the plain thing, once. If you pray, you can bring it before God.

wordCard.voice: Naaman. A proud general who wanted a grand cure, nearly walked away, and was healed by washing in the Jordan, on the word of people with no rank.

orig.note: Hebrew: wash! the servants' word to Naaman: wash, and be clean (2 Kings 5:13).

carryVoice: Your line: just wash. Seven dips in a plain river, and a proud man made clean. See you tomorrow.
